sources.title: Simo Särkkä and Lennart Svensson, Bayesian Filtering and Smoothing, 2nd ed. (2023)
sources.locator: Complete 436-page author-hosted second-edition PDF inspected. Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.2, printed pp. 91–96 (PDF pp. 121–126): Definition 6.1; Properties 6.2–6.3; Example 6.4; equations (6.7)–(6.13); Theorem 6.5 and its complete proof (6.14)–(6.16).

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.1, Definition 6.1 and Properties 6.2–6.3: probabilistic state-space model, Markov states, and conditionally independent observations
contents.reason: The page defines the exact standard-Borel kernel model and RCD conventions; the source's density-based Markov formulation is used only as a classical specialization, not as a proof of general-kernel existence.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.1, Example 6.4: scalar Gaussian random walk and Gaussian observation densities
contents.reason: The B example computes one exact scalar Gaussian prediction and update by the stated density recursion and completes the square locally.

contents.name: Equations (6.7)–(6.9): state-path prior, observation likelihood, and full-path Bayes density
contents.reason: The theorem proves the recursion from the general finite-horizon kernel law; the book's product-density factorization is retained only for its dominated specialization.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.2, Theorem 6.5 and equations (6.11)–(6.13): prediction, update, and evidence normalizer
contents.reason: The item proves a measure-level kernel version of the prediction and update equations and explicitly treats finite-positive evidence and both bad-fiber fillers.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.2, discrete-state note following Theorem 6.5: integrals become finite sums for discrete states
contents.reason: The finite HMM example verifies the recursion by exact sums, including its smoothing marginal.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.2, Theorem 6.5 and equations (6.11)–(6.13): prediction, update, and evidence normalizer
contents.reason: The algorithm states the exact measure-valued prediction/update recursion. It keeps the book’s finite-positive normalization boundary and makes the predictive filler at zero/infinite evidence explicit; correctness is proved locally in thm-dominated-state-space-filtering-recursion.

sources.title: Arnaud Doucet and Adam M. Johansen, A Tutorial on Particle Filtering and Smoothing: Fifteen Years Later (version 1.1, 2012 corrections)
sources.locator: Complete 41-page version 1.1 PDF inspected. §2.1, printed pp. 2–4 (PDF pp. 4–6): hidden Markov and general state-space model, finite-state and linear-Gaussian examples, equations (3)–(7); §2.2, printed pp. 4–5 (PDF pp. 6–7): equations (8)–(13) and their density recursions; §2.3, printed pp. 5–7 (PDF pp. 7–9): full-path smoothing target and forward–backward/two-filter formulas.

contents.name: §2.1, equations (1)–(2) and Example 1: hidden Markov model kernels and the finite-state HMM specialization
contents.reason: The example supplies exact finite state and observation probabilities, then computes the filtering and smoothing distributions directly.

contents.name: §2.1, Example 2: linear-Gaussian state and observation equations
contents.reason: The example verifies a scalar Gaussian instance of the density prediction and Bayes update equations.

contents.name: Equations (3)–(7): path prior, observation likelihood, joint density, posterior density, and evidence integral
contents.reason: These formulas are the paper's density-specific counterpart; the local theorem separately proves its broader kernel statement and endpoint handling.

contents.name: §2.2, equations (8)–(10): unnormalized full-path recursion and predictive evidence
contents.reason: The local proof derives its finite-horizon identities from the ordered kernel law instead of relying on density factorization alone.

contents.name: §2.2, equations (11)–(12): marginal prediction and filtering update
contents.reason: The item proves the exact update with a jointly measurable density and explicit zero/infinite evidence behavior.

contents.name: §2.3: full trajectory smoothing conditional on all observations
contents.reason: The A definition uses the full finite-horizon state path conditional law as the smoothing target, without importing particle smoothing.

contents.name: §2.3.1, equations (14)–(15): forward-filtering/backward-smoothing recursion
contents.reason: This pair defines the full-path smoothing conditional law but does not prove a backward recursion or any particle implementation; that separate algorithmic result is assigned to the planned particle-smoothing page.

contents.name: §2.3.2, equations (16)–(18): generalized two-filter smoothing formula and backward information filter
contents.reason: The assigned exact-filtering pair makes no claim about backward information filters, artificial smoothing distributions, or two-filter identities; no such formula is used in its definitions, theorem, or examples.

contents.name: §2.2, equations (11)–(12): marginal prediction and filtering update
contents.reason: The procedure follows the survey’s prediction and marginal update equations, while the local algorithm supplies full standard-Borel kernel inputs, jointly measurable densities, explicit bad-fiber fillers, and a finite-horizon conditional-kernel theorem.

item_arguments.argument: Define filtering, predictive, initial, and full-path smoothing versions as data-indexed conditional kernels. Null-history version freedom is explicit; no density is assumed.

Construct the finite path law under AC, use finite-product standard-Borel closure and RCD existence, then factor each RCD through its standard-Borel history variable. The initial filter is μ₀ on the singleton empty history.

Define the exact finite-horizon measure-valued prediction, evidence, and update procedure for every data history. Normalize only at finite-positive evidence and use the predictive measure at zero/infinite evidence; make no computational cost claim.

Show the transition mixture is predictive, apply dominated Bayes at each fixed history, then use ordered path factorization, conditional integration, history rectangles, and π–λ uniqueness to establish the filtering identities and bad-fiber nullity.
Verify normalized counting-measure densities, calculate two filtering updates, and derive the smoothed X₁ law directly from the finite ordered path factorization.

Derive translated normal densities and the N(0,2) prediction, complete the square at y=2, evaluate finite-positive evidence using the Gaussian integral and Lebesgue dilation, and state the selected version at the probability-zero singleton.
Compute z(a)=1 and z(b)=0 under the predictive point mass, verify the algorithm’s predictive filler, and check the RCD identities for every probability assigned at null observation b.
